site.name: Chancellor Mine
overview: Chancellor Mine is a documented producer in the Jamestown Mining District west of Jamestown, where fluorite mining became an important part of Boulder County's twentieth-century mineral industry.
Federal mine investigations and U.S. Geological Survey references specifically document the Chancellor workings and its fluorite-bearing vein system.

timeline.text: The Jamestown district began producing fluorspar in the early twentieth century, adding industrial fluorite to the district's older precious- and base-metal mining history.
Fluorite mining expanded sharply in the Jamestown area. A 1949 U.S. Bureau of Mines investigation included four diamond-drill holes totaling 1,434 feet on the Chancellor deposit.
U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 223 documented the Chancellor Mine among the Front Range ore deposits and retained it as a named Jamestown-district locality.

moreHistory: The Chancellor is also recorded as Allied Jamestown in mineral-locality references. Published records identify fluorite as a major commodity and also report silver, lead, and gold at the deposit.
The U.S. Bureau of Mines' 1949 Jamestown fluorite investigation describes drilling on the Chancellor vein as part of a broader study of mine workings and fluorspar resources in the district.

A mapped U.S. Geological Survey mine feature at approximately 40.123319, -105.396661 provides a defensible site-level location. It is used as a mine-locality point rather than a claim that a particular surviving shaft or portal has been field surveyed.
